research_question: When decision accuracy is held equal on a real Kornia replay pipeline, what incremental protection is supplied by a versioned contract, and does the current v1 certificate actually detect silent executable-code drift?
claim_boundary: Posthoc/adversarial calibration on the already-known H7I Kornia pipeline. It is neither blind evidence nor a cross-framework accuracy result.

policies.dynamic_reprobe: Repeated same-context execution checks output stability and Torch RNG stability but carries no deployment artifact.
policies.output_snapshot_guard: Compares the candidate replay output on the registered witness input to a stored output digest; this is input-specific, not a source contract.
policies.lineage_v1: Uses the existing H7I ReplayLineageCertificate and child composition unchanged.
policies.measured_source_v2_candidate: Adds a measured repository HEAD plus canonical executable-callable/MRO digest to lineage_v1; caller-supplied commit strings alone are insufficient. This is a candidate mechanism, not a frozen contribution.

source_digest_requirements: Digest resolved executable callables rather than only class names or repr strings.
Measure repository HEAD from the checked-out source rather than trusting the caller.
Canonicalization must ignore comments and formatting while changing on executable AST changes.
Monkeypatches or dynamically replaced callables must either change the digest or become unsupported/unknown.
falsification_rules: If lineage_v1 admits silent executable drift, claims that v1 is source-bound must be withdrawn until a measured source binding is added.
If output_snapshot_guard covers all required drift with lower burden and no benign-control loss, the broader contract mechanism is not justified on this scope.
If measured_source_v2 rejects benign equivalent reconstruction or comment/format-only source changes, report over-invalidation rather than counting conservative rejection as success.
No policy may use the expected case label during prediction.
